clue.text: Practical and realistic — so grounded?

definitions.meaning: a sensible, unpretentious person is described this way
read literally, something brought all the way to the soil or ground has come this far

explanation.surface: Describing a sensible person, and wondering whether that makes them grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for sensible and unpretentious, and taken literally it means brought to the ground.

clue.text: Round container Crusoe finally dropped in sea

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: a letter dropped in goes into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe tosses a round container into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped in' puts E, the last letter of Crusoe, inside CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of salt water is synonymous with the sea.

clue.text: Excellent surgeon in northeast shows innocence

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation
A1 means first-rate, written AI
a vet is a veterinary surgeon

explanation.surface: A top surgeon in the north-east of England shows guilelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written as the letters AI; a vet is a veterinary surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Unworldly simplicity and lack of experience is a form of innocence.

clue.text: Construction you once put in river

indicators.note: something put in is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England
thou is the old word for you

explanation.surface: A building you once dropped into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire; thou is the archaic form of you.
explanation.definitionFit: A small building beside a main one, such as a shed or privy, is a construction.

clue.text: Stands for election in Brunswick

indicators.note: the letters lie in the middle of the place name

explanation.surface: Someone stands as a candidate in the Brunswick constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate who contests an election is said to stand, in American usage to compete.

clue.text: Swineherd always seen in celebration?

parts.note: a man who tends hogs is a hog man
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: The pig keeper is always at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish New Year's Eve festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish New Year's Eve festivities are a famous example of a celebration, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Brave daughter having lost certain female relatives?

parts.note: with no aunts, the parents' sisters, one would be aunt-less

explanation.surface: A daughter shows courage after bereavement.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word for being without aunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not intimidated by danger is fearless and brave.

clue.text: Bill to announce opera

parts.note: Bill is a short form of William
to tell is to announce or relate

explanation.surface: An instruction to announce an opera on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a programme but is the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's last opera is named after the Swiss crossbow hero.

clue.text: Arab in next to no time coming back

indicators.note: something coming back returns the way it came, so the phrase for a moment is read right to left

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment

explanation.surface: An Arab arrives back almost immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses IN A MO, the casual British phrase for 'very soon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Oman, on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab.

clue.text: Monster wants patriarch and prophet beheaded

parts.note: Levi, son of Jacob, was one of the patriarchs of the tribes of Israel

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its top, here the first letter

parts.note: Nathan was the prophet who rebuked King David

explanation.surface: A monster seeks the execution of two biblical figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the first letter of NATHAN, leaving ATHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sea beast, and by extension anything huge, is a classic monster.

clue.text: Influential France international missed in cup-tie …

indicators.note: letters missed in a word are absent from it, so they are taken out of the match

parts.note: a semi-final is a knockout tie in a cup competition
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A French international footballer was absent from a cup match, and it mattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed in' takes F and I out of SEMIFINAL, leaving SEMINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is seminal plants the seed of later developments, so it is highly influential.

clue.text: … again, but for the last time?

definitions.meaning: a weary 'one more go, and that's it' is said when something is done a final time

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: again, but this time the final one?
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link the surface to the clue before; the wordplay is independent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a further time, and is said when asking for a final repeat.

clue.text: Not to be approached — like exhausted kangaroo?

definitions.meaning: a worn-out kangaroo has no hops left in it

explanation.surface: Keep away from a worn-out kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means off limits, and literally a kangaroo with no leaps left would have none.

clue.text: Dreadful Ms Baker joins ship

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An awful Ms Baker comes aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges MS BAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on board a vessel is to set off on it.

clue.text: See animal go on rampage in bush

indicators.note: a creature on the rampage charges about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch the beast run wild in the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on rampage' rearranges ANIMAL GO.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering plant is a shrub or small tree, so it can be called a bush.

clue.text: What heavy drinker does to exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker takes up exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink alcohol habitually and to excess is the activity of a heavy drinker.

clue.text: See sprain affected winger

indicators.note: something affected is altered, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A football winger is hurt by a sprain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' is not a footballer but a bird. 'affected' rearranges SEE SPRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Perching birds, such as sparrows, belong to this order, and any bird is something with wings.

clue.text: Fouled aplenty? Referee may award this

indicators.note: a fouled line is tangled up, so these letters are messed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Plenty of fouls in a match, so the referee gives a spot-kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fouled' rearranges APLENTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee awards a spot-kick or free kick against a team that commits a foul.

clue.text: Linguist in college once moved across lake

parts.note: a poly, or polytechnic, was a type of British college before 1992

indicators.note: a piece across another spans it, holding it inside

parts.note: got can mean moved, as in got going or got away
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A language student at an old college moved across the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts L inside GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks many languages is a linguist.

clue.text: Complete from beginning to end, concealing nothing

indicators.note: a piece concealing another holds it hidden inside

parts.note: going through something means from start to finish
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A full account from start to finish, hiding nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts O inside THROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done fully and in every detail is complete.

clue.text: Man's one from Paisley

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the inside of the town name

explanation.surface: A man from the Scottish town of Paisley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea, and its letters sit inside Paisley.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an island, so the island is what Man is one of.

clue.text: Fix where your setter admits to espionage?

parts.note: the setter owning up says I am, contracted to I'm
a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation for espionage

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter confesses to spying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' and 'to' are linking words: the setter's confession reads I'M PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed or fix something firmly in place is to set it in.

clue.text: Mr Fawlty is king? Here's creature with lethal gaze!

parts.note: Basil Fawlty is the hotelier in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Hotelier Basil Fawlty crowned king, with a glare that could kill.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical serpent of legend killed with a single look.

clue.text: Her plans unexpectedly change

indicators.note: plans that turn out unexpectedly are altered, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Her plans suddenly alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like a verb but is the noun: loose coins. 'unexpectedly' rearranges HER PLANS.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for shell fragments to mean a pocketful of loose coins.

clue.text: Classic film festival admits 50, approximately

indicators.note: a piece that admits another lets it inside

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
c, for circa, means approximately

explanation.surface: A festival lets in about fifty people to see a classic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts L and C inside EID.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1961 epic starring Charlton Heston is a classic of cinema.

clue.text: Honourable in leading Tories?

parts.note: a team leading is up, ahead in the score
the Tories, Britain's Conservatives, are the political right

explanation.surface: Is there anyone honourable among the Tory leadership?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is morally straight and decent, so honourable.

clue.text: Audible drop in level

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word for a drop is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a tear is a drop from the eye

explanation.surface: A noticeable fall in a level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' looks like a fall but is a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A row or layer in a series, such as seating rows, is a level.

clue.text: Protection in flying saucer orbiting moon ultimately

indicators.note: something orbiting goes round the other piece, enclosing it
a saucer flying through the air is tossed about, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Safety aboard a UFO circling the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges SAUCER to SURACE, and 'orbiting' wraps that round the final letter of moon; 'in' stands as written at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy covering loss or damage gives financial protection.

clue.text: Wild dog making noise disappear

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
to go is to vanish or disappear

explanation.surface: A wild dog makes a racket and then vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild dog of Australia is the standard example.

clue.text: Make difference Canute couldn't?

parts.note: King Canute famously failed to hold back the incoming sea, so literally he could not reverse it; the phrase also means to alter the course of events

explanation.surface: Something the legendary king Canute failed to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute, an 11th-century king of England, is said to have commanded the sea to retreat, and it did not.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reverse the course of events, which literally is altering the flow of the sea.
